record.original_question: Consider a slotted multi-access channel in which packets have unit service time, arrivals during each slot are Poisson with parameter lambda, W_n is the number of packets in the system at the beginning of slot n, and each packet attempts transmission in slot n with probability p_n. A transmission succeeds if exactly one packet transmits, collides if two or more transmit, and is empty if none transmits. Suppose p_{n+1} may depend only on p_n and on the binary information of whether slot n contained a successful transmission. Does there exist a protocol of this form for which the Markov chain (W_n, p_n) is positive recurrent for some lambda > 0?

evidence.quote: Consider a single channel which is shared among many users and transmits packets of a single length. Assume that time is slotted and each service time is equal to the slot length. The number of packages arriving into the system during a time slot is Poisson with parameter lambda.

At the beginning of time slot n, each package is trying to be transmitted with the same probability p_n independently of everything else. If two or more packages try to transmit simultaneously, the transmissions collide and packages stay in the system and have to try again later. If there is only one transmission, then it is successful and the package leaves the system. If there are no transmissions, then the slot is empty. Denote by W_n the number of packages in the system at the beginning of nth time slot.

Assume that probabilities p_n are defined inductively and that p_{n+1} may depend only on p_n and the binary information of whether there is a successful transmission in slot n or not. Then the pairs (W_n, p_n) form a time homogeneous Markov chain. The open question is: in the class of procedures described above, does there exist a protocol which makes the Markov chain (W_n, p_n) positive recurrent (ergodic), for some positive lambda?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a slotted multi-access communication channel operating in discrete time slots n = 0, 1, 2, …. All packets have unit service time equal to one slot. The number of new packets arriving during each slot is independent and Poisson distributed with parameter λ > 0. Let W_n denote the number of packets present in the system at the beginning of slot n.

At the beginning of slot n, each packet currently in the system independently attempts to transmit with the same probability p_n ∈ (0,1). The outcome of slot n is:
- successful, if exactly one packet attempts to transmit (this packet then leaves the system);
- a collision, if two or more packets attempt to transmit (all such packets remain in the system);
- empty, if no packet attempts to transmit.

The retransmission probabilities {p_n} are defined inductively by a feedback rule of the following restricted form: p_{n+1} is a (deterministic) function of p_n and of the single bit S_n ∈ {0,1} indicating whether slot n contained a successful transmission (S_n = 1) or did not (S_n = 0). Under any such rule, the pair (W_n, p_n) forms a time-homogeneous Markov chain.

Question: Within the class of all such success-only-feedback protocols, does there exist a protocol and some λ > 0 for which the Markov chain (W_n, p_n) is positive recurrent (ergodic)?
artifact.status_search_result: A brief web search did not surface a definitive resolution of the stability question for slotted ALOHA-type protocols restricted to success-only (one-bit) feedback. Existing literature on generalized slotted-ALOHA stability typically assumes ternary feedback (idle/success/collision) or full feedback, and no explicit positive or negative resolution of the stated success-only-feedback problem was located. Status is therefore reported as unknown.

status_evidence.title: An Analysis of Generalized Slotted-Aloha Protocols
status_evidence.snippet: Analyses generalized slotted-ALOHA protocols and their stability under various feedback assumptions.
status_evidence.claim: Standard stability analyses use richer feedback than the success-only bit considered here, and do not directly resolve the stated question.
